title: Customer Service & Sales Fundamentals
description: The daily work of serving and selling at Greens: who our customers are, the nine parts of a sales call with word-for-word scripts, recommending a size, the 22-item call score sheet, walk-ins and tours, move-ins done right, web leads, honest answers to objections, rate increases and move-outs, collections with respect, difficult and unsafe situations, reviews, and twenty practice scenarios. Course 5 of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: Who calls and walks in, what they are going through, and why the first good conversation wins
The Greens service standard and the response times every site works to
The nine parts of a sales call, with sample scripts, and recommending a size instead of asking for one
The 22-item call score sheet used again in the Hands-On Check
Walk-ins, the tour route, a move-in done right, and following up on web leads within minutes
Honest answers to objections, rate increases and move-out calls
Collections with respect, under California's and Texas' collection laws
Difficult and unsafe situations, reviews, and twenty practice scenarios

questions.q: Put these parts of a storage sales call in order.
questions.explanation: The nine parts run greeting, why they called, discovery, recommend, build value, price, then close, objections, and capture and follow up. Value comes before price.

questions.q: A caller at Valley Center asks, "How late are you open?" What is the best response?
options: Give the hours and say goodbye
Give the office and gate hours, then ask whether they are looking to rent or calling about an account
Ask why they want to know before giving the hours
questions.explanation: Answer the question first, never dodge it, then ask one question that opens the conversation. Jordheim (2015) found about 90% of hours callers get only the hours.

questions.q: Which question should you never ask a storage shopper?
options: What are you planning to store?
When do you need to move in?
questions.explanation: Most shoppers cannot picture a unit size, so they guess, usually too small. Ask what they are storing, then recommend a size and say why.

questions.q: In the 2004 IntelliShop mystery-shop study of storage calls, about how many staff asked the caller to rent?
questions.explanation: Only 25.4% asked for the rental, although 92% answered professionally (IntelliShop, 12/2004). Friendly is common; asking for the rental is rare.

questions.q: A caller describes a three-bedroom house with a piano and asks for a 10x10. What do you do?
options: Explain honestly that it will not fit, recommend a 10x20 and say why, and ask about heat for the piano
Tell her to call back when she knows her size
questions.explanation: You are the expert. A three-bedroom is about a 10x20 in the size guide, and pianos are heat-sensitive. Squeezing someone into a unit that is too small causes an angry move-in day.

questions.q: Where in the call do you give the price?
options: After you build value, unless they asked for it first
questions.explanation: Price comes after value. If a caller asks the price first, give a range from Cubby and then go to discovery.

questions.q: A practice call scores 15 Yes out of 20 items that applied, and every price and fee was quoted correctly. What is the result?
options: It cannot be scored with N/A items
questions.explanation: Score = Yes divided by items that applied: 15 / 20 = 75%. The pass mark is 70%; 90% and above is excellent.

questions.q: On the call score sheet, if you did not ask whether the caller had rented before, you may mark that item N/A.
questions.explanation: N/A is only for an item that could not apply, such as a caller who said in the first sentence that they rented before. Not asking is a No.

questions.q: Which of these is a fact you should say when you quote a Greens move-in in California?
options: There is a one-time $25 admin fee and no charge to reserve
Protection is free the first month
questions.explanation: From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026: the admin fee is $25, there is no reservation fee and no deposit on new move-ins. Say that rates are reviewed over time.

questions.q: Which is the best first line when you answer a call at Greens Storage Temecula?
options: "Thank you for calling Greens Storage Temecula, this is Maria. How can I help you today?"
"Greens Storage, what size do you need?"
questions.explanation: A great greeting has the company and property name, your name and an offer to help: "Thank you for calling Greens Storage Temecula, this is Maria. How can I help you today?"

lessons.title: Greens Tenant Protection
lessons.summary: Greens' protection levels and prices, who uses what, and how to offer it at every move-in.

lessons.title: Leads and Reservations in Cubby
lessons.summary: Lead sources and statuses, holding a unit with a reservation, and follow-up tasks.

questions.q: A web reservation arrives during open hours. What is Greens' target for the first live contact?
options: By the end of the day
questions.explanation: Byrd (2021) calls 5 minutes impactful and 30 mandatory; DeFazio (2026) says by minute six they may have moved on. Greens' standard: 5 minutes, 30 at most.

questions.q: A caller says, "The place down the road is $20 cheaper." What do you say first?
options: "Their units are dirty, you'll regret it."
"That's a fair question, and I'm glad you're comparing. Can I ask a couple of things so we're comparing the same thing?"
questions.explanation: Acknowledge it without arguing. Then compare total cost and the real differences. Never criticize a competitor, and never promise a match you have not been authorized to give.

questions.q: When a caller says a competitor is cheaper, which costs should you compare honestly? Choose all that apply.
options: Whether their price is a special and when it ends
Whether protection or insurance is required
questions.explanation: Compare total cost: the special and when it ends, the admin fee, protection, any deposit and a lock. Never pass on rumors or criticize the competitor.

questions.q: A walk-in toured a 10x15, liked it, and says, "I'll think about it." What is the best next step?
options: Let them go and hope they return
Ask whether it is the size, the price or the timing, then offer a free hold, a written quote and a set follow-up time
Offer a discount on the spot
Tell them the unit will be gone tomorrow
questions.explanation: "I'll think about it" usually hides one concern. Find it, answer it, and do not let them leave with nothing: a quote sheet, contact details, a free hold and a specific callback.

questions.q: A web reservation came in 4 minutes ago and the customer does not answer your call. What do you do?
options: Wait for them to call back
Leave a short voicemail with your name, the site and a callback time, send a text and an email, and call again later
questions.explanation: Voicemail, text and email right away, then another call, a second follow-up within 24 to 48 hours, and a confirmation the day before move-in (Byrd, 2021).

questions.q: A text telling a lead about a move-in special is a marketing text and needs the customer's prior express written consent.
questions.explanation: Under the TCPA, marketing texts need prior express written consent. Honor STOP right away. Training only, not legal advice: ask your manager which messages need which consent.

questions.q: A customer rented online and moved in without speaking to anyone. What do you still owe them?
options: A check of the unit and gate code, a welcome message, and a welcome call within a day that covers the orientation
A printed copy of the full agreement by mail
questions.explanation: Online renters skip the counter orientation. The welcome call covers the due date, late fee, autopay, protection and no living in units.

questions.q: A tenant asks why there is an admin fee on her move-in. What is the best answer?
options: "The system adds it, I can't do anything."
"It's a one-time $25 charge to set up your account. You won't see it again."
"I'll waive it if you rent today."
questions.explanation: That is the wording on Greens Fees and Charges (the $25 is From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). Quote every fee up front so it is never a surprise, and never blame a system.

questions.q: A Fairfield caller says, "Your website showed a lower rate yesterday." What do you do?
options: Argue that the website is wrong
Check Cubby; if it shows the web price for that unit, honor it; if you're unsure, ask your manager
Tell them to rent online instead
questions.explanation: Never argue about a price mismatch. If Cubby shows the web price for that unit, honor it; if you're unsure, ask your manager.

questions.q: Which offer may you make without your manager?
options: A rate below the street rate in Cubby
questions.explanation: Greens charges no reservation fee (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026), so a free hold is always yours to offer. Price matches, below-street rates and waivers above your limit are your manager's call.

lessons.title: Greens Waivers, Credits and Refunds
lessons.summary: What a waive, a credit and a refund do, and who may approve each.

lessons.title: Greens Delinquency Timeline
lessons.summary: The day-by-day collections ladder Cubby runs, and what you do at each step.

lessons.title: Greens Privacy and Records
lessons.summary: Who may hear about an account, police and subpoenas, and what Greens keeps.

questions.q: A woman says her ex rents a unit at Valley Center with "half my furniture" and asks you to cut the lock. What do you say?
options: Cut it if she shows ID
Confirm the ex rents there and call him
Without confirming whether he rents there, explain that only the tenant controls access and that a court order is the path
Let her in with the master code
questions.explanation: Never confirm or deny that someone is a tenant. Only the tenant, or someone with their code and key, gets in. A court order is the path. Call the police if she threatens anyone.

questions.q: A Fairfield tenant reports his trailer lock was cut. Which response is right?
options: "You should have bought a better lock."
Secure it with a facility lock, ask him to file a police report, write an incident report, preserve footage, and explain the claim path
Show him the camera footage on your screen
questions.explanation: Empathy, a facility lock, a police report number, an incident report, footage preserved but not shared with the tenant, neighbors checked, the claim path, no admission and no blame.

questions.q: For three nights the same car has been parked late at Murrieta, and you saw a light in a unit at 6:00 AM. What do you do?
options: Document dates, times and gate activity, tell your manager, and never approach alone
Change the tenant's gate code yourself
questions.explanation: Never approach alone. Document it, tell your manager the same day, and plan any contact with backup or the police. Treat the person with dignity.

questions.q: A family member calls: her father, a tenant, died last week. She wants into his unit today. What do you do first?
options: Let her in; she is family
Offer condolences, then explain the documents needed before access: the death certificate and proof of who handles the estate
Tell her the unit will be sold
questions.explanation: Condolence first, then documents. Do not discuss the account or give access until your manager reviews them, and give the next steps in writing.

questions.q: You are alone on site and a prospect asks you to step inside a far unit with him to measure. What do you do?
options: Stay in the doorway, hand him the tape measure, keep your phone in hand, and never say you are alone
Tell him you are alone so he understands
Close the door so it is quieter
questions.explanation: Never enter a unit with a prospect or tenant. Stay in the doorway. If anything feels wrong, end the tour or offer a video tour.

questions.q: A tenant's boxes are soaked after a roof leak and she says, "You're paying for this." What do you say?
options: "I'm really sorry. Let me photograph it and get the leak reported, and I'll explain how a claim works."
questions.explanation: Empathy without admitting liability. Document, report, offer a dry unit (a concession only within authority), explain the claim path, and never promise coverage.

questions.q: A tenant arrives shouting that his gate code failed. After he finishes, what is the best next line?
options: "So you drove out and your code didn't open the gate. I'd be upset too. Let me check it now."
questions.explanation: Lower your voice, let him finish, play it back with empathy, then solve. Verify his ID before any code help.

questions.q: A caller who is not on the account asks whether her son rents a unit at Escondido. What do you say?
options: "I'm not able to share whether any person is a customer."
"Let me check and call you back with his balance."
questions.explanation: Everything about a tenant is private, including whether they rent from Greens (Greens Privacy and Records).

questions.q: A tenant who forgot her gate code calls from the gate. What must happen before you give or reset it?
options: Nothing; she knows the unit number
Confirm her identity the way Greens requires
Ask a neighbor to vouch for her
questions.explanation: A gate code is a password. Confirm identity first, every time, then give or reset it in Cubby.

questions.q: Two joint tenants are separating, and one asks when the other last visited the unit. What do you do?
options: Read the access log to her
Say you cannot share one person's visits or account details with the other, and stay neutral
Change the code so only she has access
Ask her to bring the other tenant in
questions.explanation: Never take sides, never share one person's visits with the other, and get both joint tenants' consent for account changes. If anyone is in danger, call the police.

questions.q: Vendors citing the Self Storage Association's Demand Studies (2023 and 2025) report about what share of people rent from the first facility they contact?
questions.explanation: Reported as 58% (citing the 2023 study) and 57% (citing the 2025 study). The originals are members only, so treat the number as reported. The lesson: the first good conversation usually wins.

questions.q: Before they call you, how many places has a typical storage shopper compared, according to a 2026 operator column?
questions.explanation: DeFazio (06/16/2026): shoppers research rates, reviews and photos online and have usually compared about three places before they call. The call tests you, not just the price.

questions.q: In StorageCafe's 2026 survey, what was the top single factor renters named?
questions.explanation: Price led at 28%, with location at 17%; 54% chose climate control (StorageCafe, 2026). Most renters still named something other than price as the top reason.

questions.q: How do RV and boat customers usually differ from household customers?
options: They rent year after year, care about security and access, and are less price-driven
They only rent for one month
They do not need registration or insurance
questions.explanation: Vehicle customers often rent seasonally for years and trust staff who know vehicles: length with the tongue, height, how often it goes out.

questions.q: Put the Greens recovery method in order.
questions.explanation: Hear, Own, Solve, Thank, Fix. Hear before you solve: a fix for the wrong problem is not a fix. Fix means fixing the cause, not blaming a person.

questions.q: Saying "I'm sorry this happened" to a tenant with water damage admits that Greens is legally at fault.
questions.explanation: Apologizing for the experience is always fine and is not admitting fault. Never say Greens caused it or will pay; that is not yours to say.

questions.q: A tenant asks you to waive a fee that is above your limit. What do you say?
options: "That's my manager's call. I'll ask today and call you by 4:00 PM."
questions.explanation: Know your limits on Greens Waivers, Credits and Refunds. Never promise a waive you may not give, and never blame a system. Escalate with a set callback time.

questions.q: You promised a caller an answer by 2:00 PM, and at 1:45 PM you still do not have it. What do you do?
options: Wait and call when you know
Call at 1:45 PM, say you are still checking, and give a new time
questions.explanation: A callback promise is a promise. If you cannot keep the time, call before it and set a new one. It builds trust instead of losing it.

questions.q: Where does the often-quoted "35% of calls become rentals" figure come from?
questions.explanation: It is from 2010 (Weinman, Inside Self-Storage). A 2026 vendor dataset (Swivl) found about 15% of sales calls became rentals. Always date the number.

questions.q: A 2026 vendor dataset found about 15% of sales calls became rentals but about 4% of all touchpoints. What explains the difference?
options: The denominator: counting every call, chat and visit instead of only sales calls
questions.explanation: The way you count decides the rate. Greens measures you on new-rental calls only.

questions.q: Staff should quote the statistic that storage phone conversion "fell from 65% to 57%."
questions.explanation: We could not trace that claim to any study; it looks like a mix-up with the "57% rent from the first site" figure. Do not repeat it.

questions.q: What should a voicemail to a prospect include?
options: Your first name, the site, the unit and price they asked about, your number, and when you will try again
Their full quote and the lease terms
A special that expires in an hour
questions.explanation: A specific, friendly message gets returned. Log the attempt in Cubby, then call again at the time you said.

questions.q: Which rule applies to a recorded phone line at a California site?
options: Everyone on the call must consent, so the line plays a notice that the call may be recorded
Only the caller's consent is needed
questions.explanation: California requires all parties' consent (Penal Code 632); Texas requires one party's. Training only, not legal advice: Greens decides how calls are recorded.

questions.q: Which are the four discovery questions from Ballard and Maxwell? Choose all that apply.
options: Have you ever rented storage before?
What are you planning to store?
When do you need to move in?
How long do you think you'll need it?
questions.explanation: The four questions are rented before, what you are storing, when, and how long. Never ask what size they need.

questions.q: Which is the best example of building value?
options: "You said your mom's dresser is solid wood. Our climate-controlled units keep it out of the summer heat."
questions.explanation: Value is a feature tied to something the caller said. A feature alone is a brochure.

questions.q: Which is an assumptive close?
options: "Let me know if you have questions."
"Great, let's get you set up in the 10x15. When do you want to move in? Does Saturday work?"
"Do you want to think about it?"
questions.explanation: The assumptive close acts as if they have decided and asks about details. Most storage staff never ask for the rental at all.

questions.q: A caller wants to see a unit before renting. Which close is best?
options: "I have 11:00 AM or 3:00 PM tomorrow. Which is better?"
questions.explanation: Offer a set time. In the 2004 IntelliShop study only 33% of staff asked to set an appointment, although 98% invited a visit.

questions.q: Before you hang up on a sales call, which details should be in Cubby? Choose all that apply.
options: Move-in date and the unit and price quoted
questions.explanation: Capture name, phone, email, move date, the unit quoted, the lead source and the next contact time. A gate code is only set at move-in.

questions.q: When you quote a price, you should tell the customer that rates are reviewed over time and they will get written notice before a change.
questions.explanation: Rate increases after a low first month are the industry's top complaint. Saying it up front prevents next year's angry call.

questions.q: When you are unsure between two sizes, what does the lesson recommend?
options: Pick the smaller one; it is cheaper
Go up a size and explain why
questions.explanation: DeFazio (2026): customers who doubt it will fit go shop one more place. Going up a size with a reason (a walkway, frequent access) is service, not pressure.

questions.q: Which items are good reasons to recommend climate control? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Wood, instruments, electronics, photos, documents, art and mattresses suffer in heat. Pushing climate control for lawn furniture is an add-on customers resent.

questions.q: At Greens, which site has the climate-controlled units?
questions.explanation: 549 of Escondido's 717 enclosed units carry the Climate Controlled feature (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: During discovery a Temecula contractor mentions "a couple of gas cans for the generator." What do you do?
options: Kindly explain that fuel cannot be stored and why, and confirm he will keep it elsewhere
questions.explanation: "What are you storing?" also screens for prohibited items. Explain the rule as a helpful check, not an accusation.

questions.q: Which way of offering protection is wrong?
options: Telling a real story about a neighbor's leak
Offering Greens' plan or their own policy
Calling Greens' protection plan "insurance" and saying it is required
questions.explanation: A protection plan is not insurance, and it is never described as required unless the agreement says so. Use the approved wording on Greens Tenant Protection.

questions.q: How many items are on the Greens call score sheet, and what passes?
options: 22 items, 70% of the items that applied
questions.explanation: 22 items; 70% passes and 90% is excellent (Mixon, 2020). A wrong price or fee is never a pass.

questions.q: A call that scores 95% but quoted the wrong rent is a pass.
questions.explanation: Any call that quotes a wrong price or fee, calls the plan insurance, or promises something outside your authority is not a pass, whatever the percentage.

questions.q: How does the Hands-On Check use the call score sheet?
options: Your trainer plays a caller in a mock sales call and scores you on the same 22 items
You fill it in about a coworker
questions.explanation: The Hands-On Check's first sign-off is a mock sales call scored with this exact sheet: 70% of the items that applied, with no wrong price or fee.

questions.q: What is the mystery-shop standard for closing walk-ins who come in to rent?
questions.explanation: Mixon (2020): close 90% of walk-ins who come in to rent. Someone who drove to the site is close to renting.

questions.q: On a tour at Escondido, where do you stand when you show the unit?
options: Inside the unit, so they follow you in
In the doorway; they step in while you stay outside
questions.explanation: Never enter a unit with a prospect or tenant. Older sales advice says to step in first; Greens does not.

questions.q: Put the tour route in order.
options: Before: pick the route and check the unit
At the gate: practice the keypad
On the way: point out carts and loading
At the unit: try the latch, place their things
questions.explanation: Before, at the gate, on the way, at the unit, and the close at the unit, while they are picturing their things inside.

questions.q: A walk-in is not ready to rent. Which should you do before they leave? Choose all that apply.
options: Tell them the price goes up tomorrow
questions.explanation: Mees (2020) found no written quote and no contact capture among the top walk-in failures. Never invent urgency.

questions.q: You are alone late in the day and do not feel right about walking a prospect to the back of the property. What may you do?
options: Offer a video of the unit now and a tour when a coworker is in
questions.explanation: Trust your instincts. You may end a tour or offer a video tour instead. Never say you are alone.

questions.q: When should you confirm a move-in?
questions.explanation: Byrd (2021): confirm the arrival time the day before. It also catches plans that changed.

questions.q: At a Greens California site, which explanation of rent and late fees is correct?
options: Due on the 15th; late fee on the 16th
Due on the 1st; a late fee posts on the 11th if rent is still unpaid
questions.explanation: From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026: rent is due on the 1st and the late fee posts at 12:00 AM on the 11th. The amount is on Greens Fees and Charges.

questions.q: Which line should every new tenant hear about access?
options: "We keep a key to your lock."
"Whoever has your gate code and key can come and go until you change your code or lock."
"We let your family in if they ask."
"Only the manager can open your unit."
questions.explanation: The tenant controls access with their code and key. That rule is what makes "let me into that unit" an easy no later.

questions.q: A Temecula boat owner says his homeowner's policy covers everything. What do you do?
options: Ask him to check it covers the boat in storage, and record the policy number and expiration date in Cubby
Make him buy Greens' plan anyway
Tell him vehicles need no coverage
questions.explanation: Vehicle tenants carry their own policy. Record proof in Cubby; Cubby raises a reminder task if proof is missing or expired.

questions.q: Which Cubby lead source is a warm lead you should call the same day?
questions.explanation: An abandoned checkout was minutes from renting online. Call the same day and offer to help finish.

questions.q: A web lead arrives at 8:50 PM, after the office closed. When do you call?
options: First thing the next business morning, before the task list
questions.explanation: The office is closed; after-hours leads are the first call of the next business morning.

questions.q: Which is a good first text to a lead?
options: "Hi Joe, it's Ana at Greens Storage Temecula. Thanks for your reservation! Is now a good time to confirm your space fits your boat?"
questions.explanation: Say who you are and the site, keep it short, ask one question. Never put a balance in a text unless policy says so.

questions.q: An online reservation is for a 5x10, and the caller says she is storing a one-bedroom apartment. What do you do?
options: Explain it will not fit and move the reservation to the right size, such as a 10x10
questions.explanation: Online renters pick their own size and often pick too small. The first call confirms the size fits.

questions.q: A caller opens with, "How much is a 10x10?" What is the best response?
options: Refuse to say until they visit
Give a range from Cubby, then ask what they are storing
questions.explanation: Weinman (2010): ask about needs before price. Give the range so you are not dodging, then one discovery question.

questions.q: A Temecula boat owner asks you to match a competitor's lower price. Your manager has not authorized matches. What do you say?
options: "Price matching is my manager's call. Let me ask today and call you back by 3:00 PM."
questions.explanation: Price matches are above your authority unless your manager says otherwise. Never promise one, and never criticize the competitor.

questions.q: Which statement creates honest urgency?
options: "This is my last unit" when it is not
"Your move is Saturday. Let's make sure this unit is yours."
"Someone else is about to take it" when nobody is
questions.explanation: Urgency tied to the customer's own date is honest. Invented scarcity is a lie and a future bad review.

questions.q: A tenant says, "That late fee isn't fair. I always pay." What is the best response?
options: Empathize, explain when it applied, check your waiver authority, and offer autopay going forward
Waive it without checking your limit
questions.explanation: Use the authority on Greens Waivers, Credits and Refunds with a real reason in Cubby, or escalate with a time. Autopay prevents the next one.

questions.q: A tenant emails a move-out notice. What is Greens' standard?
options: A live phone call within 24 hours to learn why and help if you can
questions.explanation: Call live within 24 hours. Offer a save only when it fits; most move-outs are happy endings.

questions.q: A Valley Center tenant gives notice because her mother's furniture was sold. What do you do?
options: Push a discount to keep her
Thank her, confirm the steps (date, broom-clean, lock removed), and ask for a review and a referral
questions.explanation: No save fits a life change that is over. Make the move-out a happy ending.

questions.q: During a rate-increase call, when may you tell the tenant their new rate is still below the street rate?
options: Only when Cubby shows it is true
questions.explanation: Compare to the street rate only if it is true. Check Cubby first.

questions.q: A tenant asks how much notice Greens must give before a rate change. You have not read it in her agreement. What do you do?
options: Check the agreement or ask your manager before answering
questions.explanation: Notice periods come from the agreement and state law. We have not confirmed one statute for storage in California or Texas. Never guess.

questions.q: Before telling a caller their balance, what must you do?
options: Confirm they are the tenant or listed on the account, the way Greens requires
Ask for their unit number only
questions.explanation: Confirm identity first (Greens Privacy and Records). An alternate contact receives lien notices but is not entitled to account details unless also authorized.

questions.q: Which laws likely apply to how Greens collects its own rent, so Greens trains debt-collection conduct everywhere?
options: California's Rosenthal Act and Texas Finance Code chapter 392
questions.explanation: The FDCPA mostly covers third-party collectors. The Rosenthal Act (Civil Code 1788) and Texas Finance Code ch. 392 reach creditors; confirm with counsel. Training only, not legal advice.

questions.q: You call a tenant about past due rent and her roommate answers: "What's it about?" What do you say?
options: "It's a personal matter. Please ask her to call Lee at Greens Storage at this number."
questions.explanation: Third parties get your first name, Greens Storage and a callback number only, never the reason or the balance.

questions.q: Which collections voicemail is correct?
options: "This is Greens. You owe $240 and your unit goes to lien Friday."
"Hi, this is Lee from Greens Storage. Please call me back at [number]. Thank you."
"Pay now or we cut your lock."
questions.explanation: Voicemail: name, company and number only. Someone else may hear it.

questions.q: What are Greens' calling hours for collections?
options: 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM in the tenant's local time
questions.explanation: Call only between 8:00 AM and 9:00 PM local time, not at work if they object, and never to annoy. More than 7 calls in 7 days is an absolute ceiling.

questions.q: A tenant asks why you cannot take a partial payment to stop the process. Which answer is honest?
options: "A partial payment is welcome, but the account stays past due until everything is paid, so the next steps can still happen."
questions.explanation: Never blame the system. Tell the truth: Cubby applies money to the oldest charge first, and only payment in full stops the ladder (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: A coworker suggests telling a past-due tenant "we're selling Monday" when the sale is weeks away. Why is that wrong?
options: It is fine if it works
It is a false statement and a threat of something not about to happen, which collection laws forbid
questions.explanation: No false statements, no fake urgency, and never threaten action Greens does not intend or may not take. Give the real date.

questions.q: A Murrieta tenant who is 20 days late says he lost his job and can pay half today. What is the best approach?
options: Confirm identity, show empathy, take the half today, say honestly that a partial payment does not stop the next steps, and ask your manager about a plan for the rest
Agree to a payment plan for the rest on your own
questions.explanation: Empathy is not waiving everything. Take what he can pay, be honest that only payment in full stops the ladder, and escalate a plan to your manager with a callback time. Log it in Cubby.

questions.q: Which should make you stop collecting and call your manager the same day? Choose all that apply.
options: The tenant says they are on active military duty
The tenant disputes the balance in writing
The tenant promises to pay Friday
questions.explanation: Military status, bankruptcy, a death, a written dispute, a written request to stop contact, a Declaration in Opposition or a lawyer all go to your manager the same day.

questions.q: A tenant whose gate code stopped working on the 11th asks, "Is that even legal?" What do you do?
options: Explain that the law requires it
Do not defend the timing as law; give the amount needed to restore access and offer to connect her with your manager
questions.explanation: The day-11 gate code change is what Cubby does today and is under review with counsel. Never defend it to a tenant as the law; send disputes to your manager.

questions.q: Which is the right way to set a limit with a shouting customer?
options: "I'm happy to keep talking, but I can't continue if we move to yelling or insults."
questions.explanation: Set the limit calmly (Williams, 2022). If there is a threat or a safety concern, call 911.

questions.q: After a break-in, the tenant asks to see the camera footage. What do you say?
options: Explain that footage is preserved and goes to the police under Greens' policy
questions.explanation: Preserve footage and gate logs, do not promise what they show, and do not share footage directly with the tenant.

questions.q: A locked-out tenant lost the key to her own lock. What do you do?
options: Cut it for anyone who knows the unit number
Verify her photo ID against the lease, then follow Greens' steps to cut the lock and record it
Tell her to break it herself
questions.explanation: Cut a lock only for the verified tenant, with policy steps and any fee, recorded in Cubby.

questions.q: Which is a warning sign that someone may be living in a unit?
options: A tenant visits once a month
Extension cords running into a unit and the same code used very late and very early
questions.explanation: Other signs: a car parked overnight repeatedly, people walking the site after hours, a door partly open from inside. Never approach alone.

questions.q: A man who is not a tenant becomes aggressive at a Texas site and threatens you. What do you do?
options: Keep the counter between you, never say you are alone, and call 911
Give him what he asks for
questions.explanation: Any threat or safety concern: call 911. A complaint can wait; your safety cannot.

questions.q: A coworker wants to give $10 off next month to every tenant who posts a five-star review. What is the rule?
options: Not allowed: the FTC's 2024 rule bans buying positive reviews, and Greens offers no incentives at all
Allowed if the manager writes the review
questions.explanation: The FTC rule (finalized 08/2024) bans incentives conditioned on positive reviews. Greens goes further: no incentives of any kind.

questions.q: A one-star review says, "They sold my stuff." Which reply is right?
options: "You were sent three notices and were 90 days late."
"I'm sorry for how difficult this situation has been. I'm not able to discuss account details here, but I'd welcome a call at [number]."
questions.explanation: Calm, short, empathetic, no account or lien details, and take it offline. Tell your manager the same day.

questions.q: Asking only the customers you know are happy to leave a review is a good way to grow your rating.
questions.explanation: That is review gating. Ask every customer the same neutral way, good or bad.

questions.q: A 10-year-old offers to translate lease terms for her Spanish-speaking parents at a Texas site. What do you do?
options: Thank her, and bring in a Spanish-speaking teammate or Greens' approved translation help for the lease terms
questions.explanation: Never use a child to interpret lease, lien or collections terms. Use a Spanish-speaking teammate, approved help and Greens' Spanish materials.

questions.q: A Spanish-speaking customer asks whether she can have the rental agreement in Spanish. What do you say?
options: Do not promise a translated contract; ask your manager
Use an online translator on the agreement
questions.explanation: California Civil Code 1632 may require a translated contract in some cases; whether it covers storage is for counsel. Training only, not legal advice: ask your manager.

questions.q: When you practice a scenario with a coworker, what should the scorer give you afterward?
options: A list of everything you did wrong
The score and two things to work on
questions.explanation: Two things to work on, never ten. Then read "what great looks like" together and swap roles.

questions.q: A caller asks only, "How late are you open?" After you give the hours, what do you ask next?
options: "Are you looking at renting a unit, or can I help you with your account?"
questions.explanation: Ask why they called: "Are you looking at renting a unit, or can I help you with your account?" It turns an hours call into a conversation.
